questions.question: Which of the following tribe belongs to Indo-European Linguistic family?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhili**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhili:-**

 
 
• **The Bhil are one of the largest tribal groups in India, primarily residing in the states of Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.**
 
• **They belong to the Indo-European Linguistic family.**
 
• They are also found in smaller numbers in Tripura, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Bhil tribes are mainly concentrated in the districts of Dhar, Jhabua, and West Nimar of Madhya Pradesh, and in Banswara and Chittorgarh districts of Rajasthan. A significant population also resides in the easternmost districts of Gujarat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Korwa:-**

 
 
• **The Korwa is an indigenous tribe largely found in the Indian states of Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Odisha. **
 
• Although they are spread across numerous states, their population is relatively small compared to other tribes.
 
 
 
• **Gondi:-**
 
 
• **The Gondi people are one of the largest Adivasi, or tribal groups, in India. **
 
• They are primarily found in the central region of India, within the states of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Garo:-**
 
 
• **The Garo are one of the major tribal communities in North-East India, predominantly inhabiting the Indian states of Meghalaya, Assam, and Tripura. **
 
• There are also Garo communities living in parts of Bangladesh adjacent to the Indian border.

questions.question: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 declares the instant divorce granted by pronouncement of talaq three times as void and illegal. It provides for imprisonment for a term up to _________ and fine to the husband who practiced instant Triple Talaq.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019:-**

 
 
• It protects Married Women.
 
• The act takes all declarations of talaq, including in written or electronic form, to be void.
 
• **The act makes declaration of talaq a cognizable offence, attracting up to three years’ imprisonment with a fine. (Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
• Under this act, only Magistrate can grant bail to the accused.
 
• If the Women requests, then the offence may be compounded by the Magistrate.
 
• The custody of the minor children will also be determined by the Magistrate.
 
• Muslim women are entitled to seek Subsistence Allowance.
 
• **The Act renders instant triple talaq illegal and void, and also provides for maintenance to the woman and her dependent children. **
 
• This law was developed following a landmark 2017 ruling by the Supreme Court of India that found the practice of instant triple talaq unconstitutional.

questions.question: The last Mughal Emperor who was sent to Jail in Rangoon was _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah Zafar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar:-**

 
 
• He was the last Mughal emperor of India.
 
• He reigned from 1837 to 1857. Born on October 24, 1775, Bahadur Shah was the son of Akbar Shah II and Lalbai, who was a Hindu Rajput.
 
• **After the crushing of the rebellion, the British exiled him to Rangoon, Burma, now known as Yangon, Myanmar. (Hence option 4 is correct).**
 
• In 1862, he died there at the age of 87. Despite the dire conditions of his end, Bahadur Shah Zafar remains a notable figure and symbol of resistance against British colonial rule.
 
• His tomb in Yangon has become a shrine for Indians living in the city.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ​Alamgir II:**

 
 
• ​Alamgir II was the Mughal emperor of India from 1754 to 1759.
 
• He was the son of Jahandar Shah, who was the fourth son of Bahadur Shah I.
 
• Alamgir II was not the direct successor of his father as he was imprisoned by his uncle, Ahmad Shah Bahadur, who became the emperor after Jahandar Shah.
 
 
 
• **Shah Alam II:-**
 
 
• **Shah Alam II was the Mughal Emperor of India who ruled from 1759 to 1806.**
 
• He was the son of Alamgir II and the grandson of Jahandar Shah.
 
• Shah Alam II's reign was marked by political instability and conflict with various regional powers, including the Maratha Empire, the British East India Company, and the Rohilla Afghans.
 
 
 
• **Akbar shah II:-**
 
 
• Akbar II granted the title of 'Raja' to the famous social and cultural reformer Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• He is credited with starting the Hindu-Muslim unity festival Phool Walon Ki Sair.
 
• **Akbar had little de facto power due to the increasing British influence in India through the East India Company.**
 
• Akbar Shah II reigned from 1806 to 1837.

questions.question: FIFA World Cup is associated with ________ sport.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Football.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **FIFA World Cup:-**

 
 
• **The FIFA World Cup is an international association football competition between the senior men's national teams of the members of the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), the sport's global governing body. **
 
• The tournament has been held every four years since the inaugural tournament in 1930, with the exception of 1942 and 1946 due to the Second World War.
 
• The reigning champions are Argentina, who won their third title at the 2022 tournament. 
 
• The World Cup has been won by eight different teams, with Brazil having the most titles with five. Other successful teams include Germany and Italy with four titles each, Argentina and Uruguay with three titles each, and France and England with one title each.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

• Headquarters: Zurich, Switzerland.
 
• President: Gianni Infantino.
 
• Secretary-General: Fatma Samba Diouf Samoura
 
• Founded: 21 May 1904​

questions.question: The terms Kumi-Kata, Shintai, Ukemi are associated with which sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Judo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judo**:-

 
 
• **Judo is a Japanese martial art that originated in the late 19th century.**
 
• It was developed by Jigoro Kano, who was a practitioner of Ju-jitsu, a traditional Japanese martial art.
 
• Ju-jitsu is a close-combat fighting system that originated in feudal Japan and was used by the samurai.
 
• Judo is based on the principles of Ju-jitsu but emphasizes throws, pins, and joint locks rather than strikes and kicks.
 
• Judo became an Olympic sport in 1964 and is now practiced worldwide.
 
• **The terms Kumi-Kata, Shintai, Ukemi are associated with Judo.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Polo

 
 
• Polo, game played on horseback between two teams of four players each of who uses mallets with long, flexible handles to drive a wooden ball down a grass field and between two goalposts.
 
• It is the oldest of equestrian sports.
 
• A game of Central Asian origin, polo was first played in Persia (Iran) at dates given from the 6th century BC to the 1st century AD.
 
 
 
• **Fencing**:-
 
 
• It is an intriguing sport with roots dating back centuries.
 
• **It originated as a form of sword fighting among European nobility, and over time, it has evolved into a competitive sport that tests physical fitness, speed, agility, and strategic thinking.**
 
 
 
• **Wrestling**:-
 
 
• Wrestling is a popular sport in India and has a rich history.
 
• **It is believed to have originated in the Indus Valley Civilization around 5000 years ago.**
 
• India has produced many legendary wrestlers in the past, including the likes of Dara Singh, Sushil Kumar, and Yogeshwar Dutt.

questions.question: Islamic style of architecture is also known as ________ style.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mehrab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mehrab**:-

 
 
• **It is a niche in the wall of a mosque that indicates the direction of prayer towards Mecca, is a central and iconic feature of Islamic architecture.**
 
• The mihrab is often decorated with intricate geometric designs, calligraphy, and other forms of ornamentation.
 
• It is a symbol of the unity of the Muslim community and the importance of prayer in Islamic worship.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yashmak architecture:-**

 
 
• **It is a style of architecture that is characterized by its use of traditional Egyptian and Islamic elements, as well as its focus on sustainability and comfort. **
 
• Yashmak architects often use natural materials, such as mudbrick, stone, and wood, and they incorporate traditional design elements, such as arches, mashrabiyas, and courtyards. 
 
 
 
• **Hegira architecture:-**
 
 
• **It is a term used to describe the architecture of the Islamic world during the first few centuries after the Hijra, the migration of the Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE. **
 
• This period was marked by a great deal of innovation and experimentation in architecture, as Muslims sought to create new building forms that reflected their unique religious and cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Alim architecture:-**
 
 
• **It is a relatively new style of architecture that is characterized by its use of computational design, advanced materials, and sustainable practices. **
 
• Alim architects often use computer-aided design (CAD) and building information modeling (BIM) software to create complex and innovative building forms.

questions.question: All human beings have ________ pairs of chromosomes in the nuclei of their cells.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chromosomes**:-

 
 
• Chromosomes are thread-like structures located inside the nucleus of animal and plant cells.
 
• **Each chromosome is made of protein and a single molecule of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA). **
 
• DNA contains the genetic information that makes each living thing unique.
 
• **Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46 chromosomes in each cell. (Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• The first 22 pairs are called autosomes, and they look the same in both males and females.
 
• The 23rd pair is the sex chromosomes, which determine a person's sex. Females have two X chromosomes, while males have one X and one Y chromosome.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps our body to use calcium for bones and teeth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Vitamin D:-**

 
 
• Vitamin D is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays a vital role in calcium absorption and bone health.
 
• It helps to transport calcium from the intestines to the bloodstream and into the bones.
 
• Vitamin D also helps to produce osteocalcin, a protein that helps to build and maintain strong bones.
 
• **Vitamin D helps our body to use calcium for bones and teeth.**
 
• Good sources of vitamin D include sunlight, fatty fish such as salmon and tuna, eggs, and fortified milk and cereals. It is also possible to take a vitamin D supplement.

questions.question: Minal wrote an essay on the largest moon of Saturn. Which among the following moons is it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Titan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Titan:-**

 
 
• **It is the second-largest moon in the Solar System, after Jupiter's moon Ganymede. **
 
• It is also the only known moon in the Solar System to have a dense atmosphere, and the only known world besides Earth on which clear evidence of stable bodies of surface liquid has been found.
 
• **Titan's atmosphere is primarily made of nitrogen, with a small fraction of methane. **
 
• The dense atmosphere frequently produces bright white convective clouds, especially over the south pole region. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carme:-**

 
 
• **It is a retrograde irregular satellite of Jupiter. **
 
• It was discovered by Seth Barnes Nicholson at Mount Wilson Observatory in California in July 1938.
 
• It is named after the mythological Carme, mother by Zeus of Britomartis, a Cretan goddess.
 
 
 
• **Atlas:-**
 
 
• **It is a small inner moon of Saturn. **
 
• It was discovered in 1980 by Richard Terrile from Voyager photos and was designated S/1980 S 28. 
 
 
 
• **Europa:-**
 
 
• **It is one of the most intriguing moons in the Solar System. **
 
• It is the sixth-largest moon in the Solar System and the fourth-largest of Jupiter's moons.
 
• Europa is slightly smaller than Earth's Moon, but it is more massive than all known moons in the Solar System smaller than itself combined.

questions.question: Who administers the Union Territories of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• President:

 
 
• Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Constitution deal with the Union executive.
 
• The Union executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the council of ministers and the attorney general of India.
 
• The president is elected not directly by the people but by members of electoral college consisting of:
 
 
• the elected members of both the Houses of Parliament;
 
• the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states; and
 
• the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry
 
 
 
• The president administers the Union Territories of India.
 
• The President’s election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting is by secret ballot.
 
• The President holds office for a term of five years.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chief Minister

 
 
• He is the head of the state government.
 
• Governor appoints Chief Minister.
 
• The chief minister is elected through a majority in the state legislative assembly.
 
• The tenure of the Chief Minister is not fixed and he holds his office at the pleasure of the Governor.
 
• He is a member of the Inter-State Council and National Development Council which are headed by the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• Prime Minister of India:
 
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and other ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• The Prime Minister of India is the Head of the Government of India.
 
• He is also the head of the council of ministers.
 
• He is the chairman of the cabinet and presides over the meetings of the Cabinet.
 
• He acts as the chief advisor to the President of India.
 
• The Prime Minister submits his resignation to the President of India.
 
 
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs):
 
 
• MLAs are elected by the people. 
 
• They then become members of the legislative assembly and also form the government.
 
• In this way we say that the MLAs represent people.

questions.question: 'Romancing with Life' is an autobiography of the evergreen star ________.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-cooperation Movement in February 1922 after which incident?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chauri Chaura Incident**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chauri Chaura incident:-**

 
 
• On February 5, 1922, a mob of protesters participating in the Non-cooperation Movement at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh, India, clashed with the police.
 
• The protesters set fire to the police station, killing 22 policemen.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-cooperation Movement in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident. (Hence option 1 is correct)**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh massacre:-**

 
 
• It was also known as the Amritsar massacre, took place on April 13, 1919, in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, Punjab, British India. 
 
 
 
• **Kakori train robbery:-**
 
 
• **It was an armed robbery that took place on August 9, 1925, on a train in central Uttar Pradesh, India. **
 
• It was organized by the Indian revolutionaries of Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
 
 
• **Bomb Blast in central assembly:-**
 
 
• On April 8, 1929, a bomb exploded in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi, India.
 
• **The bomb was thrown by Bhagat Singh, a member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). **
 
• The bomb blast was intended to protest against the British rule in India.

questions.question: Which famous ruler was known as the "Second Ashoka"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanishka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanishka**:-

 
 
• Kanishka was the most well-known and greatest king among all the Kushana kings.
 
• Kanishka founded the Saka era (78 AD).
 
• **He was known as the "Second Ashoka".**
 
• Kanishka was a follower of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• The fourth Buddhist Council was held during Kanishka's reign.
 
• Mathura and Gandhara's school of art flourished during his reign.

• Chandragupta II

 
 
• One of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II, also known by his given name Vikramaditya and Chandragupta Vikramaditya.
 
• He was the third ruler of the Gupta Empire in India.
 
• The famous Chandragupta II was the child of Samudragupta and Datta Devi.
 
 
 
• **Milinda:-**
 
 
• **He was a Greco-Bactrian king who ruled a large territory in the Northwestern regions of the Indian Subcontinent from his capital at Sagala. **
 
• Menander is noted for having become a patron and convert to Greco-Buddhism and he is widely regarded as the greatest of the Indo-Greek kings.

questions.question: Which among the following is a noble chemical element of science periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium**:-

 
 
• **It is a noble chemical element with the symbol He and atomic number 2. **
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless, non-toxic, inert, monatomic gas and the first in the noble gas group in the periodic table.
 
• Its boiling point is the lowest among all the elements, and it does not have a melting point at standard pressure. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cobalt:-**

 
 
• **It is a chemical element with the symbol Co and atomic number 27. **
 
• It is a hard, silvery-white metal that is ferromagnetic (meaning it is attracted to magnets).
 
• Cobalt is found naturally in the Earth's crust and is mined from cobalt ore.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen:-**
 
 
• **It is a chemical element with the symbol N and atomic number 7. **
 
• It is a nonmetal and the lightest member of group 15 of the periodic table, often called the pnictogens.
 
• It is a common element in the universe, estimated at seventh in total abundance in the Milky Way and the Solar System.
 
 
 
• **Scandium:-**
 
 
• **It is a chemical element with the symbol Sc and atomic number 21. **
 
• It is a silvery-white metal that is lightweight and strong.
 
• Scandium is rare in nature and is found in small amounts in over 800 minerals.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Mass Media?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**door to door campaign.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Door-to-door campaign:-**

 
 
• **It is a method of canvassing in which campaign workers go from house to house to talk to voters.**
 
• This can be done for a variety of purposes, such as to raise awareness of a cause or candidate, to collect signatures for a petition, or to register people to vote. 
 
• Door-to-door campaigns can be very effective, as they allow campaign workers to have direct conversations with voters and to learn about their concerns.
 
• However, they can also be time-consuming and challenging, as it can be difficult to get people to answer their doors or to listen to what you have to say.
 
• **It is not an example of Mass Media.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newspapers**:-

 
 
• **These are periodicals that contain written information about current events. **
 
• They are typically published on a daily or weekly basis, and they cover a wide range of topics, including politics, business, sports, art, and science. 
 
 
 
• **Television**:-
 
 
• **It is a telecommunication system for transmitting moving images and sound from a distance. **
 
• It is a form of mass media that has had a profound impact on society. 
 
 
 
• **Radio**:-
 
 
• It is a technology that uses radio waves to transmit audio signals between two points.
 
• **It is one of the oldest and most popular forms of mass media.**

questions.question: Which layer of the soil has maximum concentration of humus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Top Soil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Top Soil:-**

 
 
• **The layer of soil with the maximum concentration of humus is the topsoil. **
 
• The topsoil is the topmost layer of soil, and it is made up of a mixture of organic matter and mineral matter.
 
• The organic matter in the topsoil comes from decaying plant and animal matter, and it is this organic matter that gives the topsoil its dark color and its nutrient-rich properties.
 
• The amount of humus in the topsoil varies depending on a number of factors, including the type of vegetation that grows in the area, the climate, and the management practices used on the land. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Soil is a complex mixture of minerals, organic matter, water, and air.
 
• It is essential for life on Earth, as it provides plants with the nutrients they need to grow and reproduce.
 
• Soil also plays an important role in water filtration, climate regulation, and carbon storage.

questions.question: The Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Hardeep Singh Puri, in October 2022 inaugurated Asia's largest Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plant in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Asia's largest Compressed Bio Gas:-**

 
 
• The Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Hardeep Singh Puri, in October 2022 inaugurated Asia's largest Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) plant in Sangrur, Punjab.** (Hence option 1 is correct)**
 
• The plant is spread across an area of 20 acres and has been commissioned with an FDI investment of approximately Rs. 220 crores.
 
• The plant's present production is about 6 tonnes per day, but it will soon use 8 digesters with a combined capacity of 10,000 cubic metres to process 300 tons of paddy straw each day.
 
• The plant is expected **to generate employment for over 1,000 people **and **will help to reduce air pollution by converting agricultural waste into clean fuel.**
 
• It will also help to reduce India's dependence on imported fossil fuels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Compressed Bio Gas:-**

 
 
• **CBG plant is a facility that produces biogas and compresses it to natural gas quality.**
 
• Biogas is a renewable energy source that is produced by the anaerobic digestion of organic matter, such as agricultural waste, municipal solid waste, and sewage treatment plant waste.
